site.name: EleutherIA
site.imageAlt: EleutherIA knowledge graph for ancient free will debates
site.author: Romain Girardi
site.keywords: ancient philosophy, free will, determinism, moral responsibility, knowledge graph, GraphRAG, digital humanities, Greek philosophy, Latin texts, Stoicism, Augustine, Aristotle

routes.title: EleutherIA | Ancient Free Will Knowledge Graph
routes.description: Explore EleutherIA, a FAIR-aligned knowledge graph and AI research platform for ancient debates on free will, fate, providence, and moral responsibility.
routes.summary: EleutherIA combines ancient Greek and Latin texts, a curated knowledge graph, vectorless retrieval, and citation-grounded GraphRAG to study 1,200 years of free will debates.

routes.title: How EleutherIA Works | Knowledge Graph, Vectorless GraphRAG
routes.description: Learn how EleutherIA connects knowledge graph modeling, SQL/tree/lemma retrieval, passage citations, and GraphRAG to make ancient free will debates searchable and citable.
routes.summary: This page explains the EleutherIA research architecture: source ingestion, knowledge graph curation, vectorless retrieval, hybrid search, and a multi-stage GraphRAG pipeline.

routes.title: EleutherIA Database Overview | Ancient Free Will Knowledge Graph
routes.description: Browse the structure, corpus coverage, philosophical traditions, and FAIR data model behind the EleutherIA ancient free will database.
routes.summary: The database organizes authors, works, passages, concepts, arguments, traditions, and citations into a research-grade knowledge graph for ancient free will studies.

routes.title: Knowledge Graph Visualizer | EleutherIA
routes.description: Explore the EleutherIA knowledge graph visually, moving between philosophers, works, concepts, arguments, and source passages in ancient free will debates.
routes.summary: The visualizer lets researchers inspect the structure of the EleutherIA graph and follow relations between ancient authors, concepts, works, and debates.

routes.title: Knowledge Graph Explorer | EleutherIA
routes.description: Inspect EleutherIA's graph of ancient free will concepts, sources, philosophers, and arguments through an interactive graph exploration interface.
routes.summary: The graph explorer is an alternate entry point into the EleutherIA knowledge graph, built for inspecting relationships across the corpus.

routes.title: GraphRAG Q&A for Ancient Free Will | EleutherIA
routes.description: Ask citation-grounded research questions about ancient free will, fate, providence, and moral responsibility using EleutherIA's agentic GraphRAG system.
routes.summary: GraphRAG combines retrieval from the ancient text corpus and knowledge graph with structured reasoning to produce scholarly answers with verifiable citations.

routes.title: Agentic GraphRAG for Ancient Philosophy | EleutherIA
routes.description: See how EleutherIA's GraphRAG system grounds answers in ancient sources, graph paths, vectorless retrieval, and transparent scholarly evidence.
routes.summary: The showcase explains how the GraphRAG pipeline retrieves, reasons over, and cites ancient evidence for questions about freedom, fate, and moral agency.

routes.title: Live Research Mode | EleutherIA
routes.description: Watch EleutherIA's agentic research process assemble evidence, reason over sources, and produce transparent answers for ancient philosophy questions.
routes.summary: Live Research exposes the reasoning workflow behind longer scholarly synthesis, showing how sources and sub-questions are assembled into an answer.

routes.title: Ancient Works Library | EleutherIA
routes.description: Browse ancient Greek, Latin, and related works used by EleutherIA to study free will, fate, providence, and moral responsibility.
routes.summary: The ancient works library provides access to the primary corpus behind the knowledge graph, including classical, Hellenistic, imperial, and late antique sources.

routes.title: Bibliography on Ancient Free Will | EleutherIA
routes.description: Explore the modern scholarship cited by EleutherIA, including secondary literature on ancient philosophy, theology, determinism, and moral responsibility.
routes.summary: The bibliography records secondary scholarship used to interpret and contextualize ancient free will debates across the EleutherIA corpus.

routes.title: About EleutherIA | Romain Girardi
routes.description: Learn about EleutherIA, Romain Girardi's FAIR-aligned scholarly platform for ancient free will debates, knowledge graphs, and GraphRAG research.
routes.summary: EleutherIA is developed by Romain Girardi as a digital humanities research platform for studying ancient debates about free will, fate, and moral responsibility.

routes.title: Glossary of Ancient Free Will Terms | EleutherIA
routes.description: Definitions of the key Greek and Latin concepts in ancient debates on free will, fate, and moral responsibility: heimarmene, eph' hemin, prohairesis, synkatathesis, autexousion, liberum arbitrium, and more.
routes.h1: Key Terms in the Ancient Free-Will Debate
routes.summary: A grounded scholarly glossary of Greek and Latin terms for fate, necessity, voluntary action, assent, and free will, each defined from the EleutherIA knowledge graph with verbatim original-language forms.

routes.title: Frequently Asked Questions | EleutherIA
routes.description: Answers to common questions about EleutherIA: what the platform is, what data it contains, how its citation-grounded GraphRAG works, and key questions about ancient free will, fate, and moral responsibility.
routes.summary: Grounded answers about EleutherIA's knowledge graph, ancient text corpus, vectorless GraphRAG retrieval, open licensing, and core questions in the ancient free will debate.
